concept.title: How to read a category page
concept.shortdesc: Every category is a page of its own, with the same parts in the same order, so that a reviewer can compare them quickly.

conbody.p: The classification has three dimensions. Each one answers a separate question about a service, and a service can have a value in all three: what is offered is kept apart from who it is for and from what a person must meet to use it. The glossary entry for explains why.

section.title: The parts of a category page

dlentry.dd: The category's name, and a one-sentence definition. Both were written by a language model from the clustered phrases. A reviewer decides whether to keep, rename or reword them.
Short examples drawn from the members of the cluster. They show the range, not every case.

Things that look similar but sit elsewhere. Each links to the category it belongs in, so a reviewer can follow the boundary. Where the neighbouring group was not stable enough to be named, the page says so instead of linking.

dlentry.dt: How people might ask for it
dlentry.dd: Everyday search phrases for the category. They are also the page's search keywords.
The group the category belongs to and the dimension it is part of.
For service-type categories, the needs in the draft catalogue that name the category. The need pages link back.
How many records came from each directory, how steady the group was when the data was resampled, whether it is a single kind of thing, and any reason a person should look at it first.

ul.li: Stability is the share of resamplings in which the group re-formed, from 0 to 1. A group at 0.6 or above is treated as having recurred. A lower value means the group may be an accident of the sample.
Unconfirmed categories did not recur reliably. They have a name only because a need in the catalogue points at them, so that a stability filter cannot silently remove something people need.
Records by directory shows whether a category is one directory's habit. A category that one directory holds almost entirely is flagged.
Identifiers such as svc-044 are cluster numbers of this run. A new run renumbers them, so they are for cross-referring within this document and not for use as stable identifiers.
